body:
This PR introduces volume-per-area conserving advection as it is done in SI3. In practice, the advection operator computes the divergence of ice per area volume volume (h * \aleph) and the thickness is recovered by dividing the new volume by the new thickness. A small-concentration guard is added that zaps the ice volume to zero when the concentration is below the threshold (we loose mass, but a very tiny amount).

I also have renamed `V` to `𝓋` to indicate that what we are dealing with is not a volume (extensive property) but the volume per area, an intensive density-like variable.
title: Volume (per area)-conserving sea-ice advection

body:
The methods we have in Oceananigans for Coriolis includes a dz interpolation in the formulation. Sea-ice wants 2D coriolis, so the coriolis force is incorrect when we use zstar that modifies dz horizontally.

This PR introduces a 2D coriolis method specific to sea ice which does not include the dz.
title: Use a grid-invariant Coriolis

body:
Sea ice thickness is supposed to have a distributed within a cell, this distribution changes the denominator of the conditive flux as $$1 / < h > \neq <1 / h>$$.
This is solved in multi-category models by evolving a distributed rather that just a mean thickness.
This PR allows to introduce a discrete prescribed sea ice distribution to be able to control, also in the one-category model, the response of thin vs thick sea ice.
title: Include a prescribed distribution for sea ice thickness
